newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-YOUNG PUTS NZ IN COMMAND OF 1ST TEST.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-YOUNG PUTS NZ IN COMMAND OF 1ST TEST.

text.p: The run feast continued for New Zealand on the second morning of the first cricket test against Sri Lanka at Carisbrook on Saturday.
New Zealand resumed on 343 for four this morning and carried their score through to 433 for five by the lunch break.
Opening batsman Bryan Young, who finished the first day unbeaten on his career test best 154, was within sight of a double century at 187.
He will be joined in the afternoon by Chris Cairns, who mixed cautious defence in the morning with a willingness to punish anything loose.
Cairns was on 50, including a big six over mid wicket off left-arm seamer Chaminda Vaas which he picked up from just outside his off stump.

The only wicket to fall in the morning was that of nightwatchman Daniel Vettori, who departed on the second ball of the session for one when he edged Vaas to second slip, where Roshan Mahanama took his third catch of the innings.
Mahanama erred shortly after that, though, when he grassed a straight-forward chance at second slip off Young, who at that stage was on 155.
Vaas was the most successful bowler, with three for 120.
